$comment: CarSetup keys excluded from setup identity (values fingerprint). Derived by the sim or run readings, not user settings. Source: prove/P5 (corner weights, ride heights, ARB and truck-arm preload differ by 1 N / 1 mm / 0.2 Nm for the same file), setup_recordings.py:30-33 (run readings) and the setup harvest of 2026-10-04 (the anti-roll-bar preload is also published as a leaf named Preload in its bar's section: Chassis.FrontArb.Preload on the Supra, Tundra and Taurus, Chassis.Rear.Preload beside the Taurus's rear-bar ArbDiameter and LinkSlack; garage snapshots that differed only there were kept as setups of their own). No recorded car publishes a user-set leaf named Preload (the test-data/sdk fixture and the owner's recordings, checked 2026-10-04); a car that does needs a narrower rule. Patterns match the last path segment of a setup key, ignoring ASCII case and any '_' in the key: a CarSetup key such as Chassis.LeftFront.CornerWeight, or the canonical key of a garage .htm export such as chassis.left_front.corner_weight. Values are still stored and shown; they only do not count toward identity. Patterns stay inside a subset that consumers may match without a regular-expression engine (the collector links coach-ibt and has a 3 MB budget): a leading ^, ASCII letters and digits, at most one group (a|b|...) of such literals, which a ? after it makes optional, and an optional trailing $; a pattern always needs at least one letter outside an optional group. Change by contract review only.

fingerprint.input: for each remaining key in ascending UTF-8 byte order: key + 0x1F + raw value string exactly as published (trimmed) + 0x1E
